title: Pin cargo-nextest in athena.toml [tools] and nothing else
summary: Retry of the nextest speedup, narrowed to its first step as the introspection proposed: pin cargo-nextest by exact version in athena.toml [tools], parsed by the config. The test check, CI, docs and changelog are left to follow-up jobs. The audience is the user, who judges this by the tools table and clean checks.

defaults_applied.how: Only the pin and the config field that parses it; every other surface of the original job is deferred.
A config test covers the new pin, and cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
A criterion checks that the real athena.toml parses with the nextest pin, not just that the line exists.
Adopts the existing cargo-nextest tool instead of building a runner.
The config uses deny_unknown_fields, so the pin is enforced by parsing.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Tools in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs allows only gitleaks (archive sha256 pin) and an optional sccache (CratePin: version only, built by cargo install --locked). I assume nextest follows the sccache precedent: an optional CratePin, because a producer in a sandbox probably cannot download a release archive to compute a real checksum, and a made-up checksum is worse than none.
If the producer can fetch a real archive checksum, it may use a ToolPin instead; it must never invent a digest.
The version is a real released cargo-nextest version the producer can confirm from the repository or Cargo registry data; if it cannot confirm one, it stops and reports that rather than guessing.
Nothing may use the pin yet: the test check, ci.yml, setup.sh, docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md stay unchanged.
Governance file athena.toml is named as a deliverable and in a criterion.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml has a [tools] entry for cargo-nextest with an exact version (no range), and any checksum in it is a real value for a real release archive, not a placeholder.
The Tools struct in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs accepts the nextest pin, and a unit test shows the repository's real athena.toml parses with that pin present.
The test check, ci.yml, docs/decisions.md, CHANGELOG.md and the capability env tables are unchanged.
Run `cargo test --locked`: it passes, including the existing config and tools tests and the new nextest pin test.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`: both are clean.

out_of_scope: Switching the test check to nextest or running cargo test --doc separately
ATHENA_HOME in capability env tables and runner reporting
Nextest output parsing in checks.rs and gh.rs
departures: Narrower than the original, so slightly higher pass odds; the pin version and checksum are unverifiable offline, which keeps the odds below high.
urgent_reason: Splitting the job into a small pin job cuts the redo work of a producer that made no change on a six-surface request.
